evals.prompt: Help me create a LinkedIn content strategy. I'm a SaaS founder building in public and want to grow my personal brand to drive awareness for my product. I currently have 500 followers and post maybe once a week.
evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing.md first. Should propose a manageable 3–5-pillar starting set for the founder, justified by audience coverage and production capacity. It should read current LinkedIn guidance and the account's last 30–90 days before naming a cadence, format, or time. If those data are unavailable, it should label 2–4 posts per week for four weeks as a starting hypothesis, rotate at least two formats and audience-local windows, and define the metrics that will decide the next cadence. It should provide hook options, a test calendar, a capacity-bounded engagement routine, and a batching plan without claiming carousels, stories, or more posting will automatically perform better.
assertions: Labels cadence and format ranges as testable starting hypotheses

evals.prompt: Write me a Twitter/X thread about the lessons I learned bootstrapping my SaaS to $10k MRR. Include hooks and a CTA at the end.
evals.expected_output: Should verify that the claimed MRR and timeline are source-backed, then structure a coherent thread with an opening promise, evidence, lessons, and one CTA. It should choose the number of posts needed to deliver the proof without padding; when no account evidence exists, a 5–9-post draft is an explicit starting hypothesis with a compression option. It should reference the founder-journey pillar and include a relevant response prompt without claiming a universal platform best practice.
assertions: Applies hook formulas from the skill
Uses a story hook for the first tweet
Structures thread with standalone but flowing tweets
Uses an evidence-dependent thread length without padding

evals.prompt: i have a blog post that did really well. how do i turn it into social media content for multiple platforms?
evals.expected_output: Should trigger on casual phrasing and apply the content repurposing system. It should treat platform formats, extraction count, link placement, and distribution timing as starting hypotheses to verify against current official guidance, account results, source richness, and approval capacity. It should adapt each candidate asset to its platform, return drafts for exact-content approval, and define what evidence will decide the next batch.
assertions: Uses Blog Post → Social Content mapping
Provides format for LinkedIn, Twitter/X, and Instagram

evals.prompt: My LinkedIn posts get like 200 impressions and almost no engagement. What am I doing wrong?
evals.expected_output: Should request the account's recent reach, dwell or retention, replies, follows, format, timing, audience, and post samples before diagnosing. It should frame hooks, timing, formatting, topic fit, and participation as hypotheses, then propose a one-variable-at-a-time test across comparable posts. If account insights are unavailable, it should provide a manual worksheet and two bounded format and timing tests. It should provide before-and-after hook examples without promising higher reach.
assertions: Recommends a measurable capacity-bounded participation test

evals.prompt: Help me reverse-engineer what's working for top creators in the DevTools space on Twitter. I want to understand their content patterns.
evals.expected_output: Should apply the reverse-engineering framework using a bounded sample of comparable DevTools accounts selected by audience, offer, account maturity, and available metrics. It should discover currently callable authorized collection tools and source terms; when none are available, it should provide a manual spreadsheet and work from user-supplied URLs or exports. It should add accounts and posts until another batch no longer changes the leading patterns rather than hard-code a sample size. It should analyze hooks, formats, CTAs, topics, timing, reach, and downstream actions only where the platform exposes them, then codify hypotheses and layer the user's voice.
assertions: Applies the evidence-based content pattern framework
Walks through the full process (find, collect, analyze, codify, apply)
Builds a bounded comparable sample and stops at pattern saturation

evals.prompt: Write me a 5-email welcome sequence for new email subscribers who came from my LinkedIn audience.
evals.expected_output: Should recognize this is an email sequence task, not social content. Should defer to or cross-reference `suede-emails`, which handles welcome sequences, drip campaigns, and lifecycle emails. May note the social-to-email bridge context but should make clear that `suede-emails` is the right skill for writing email sequences.
assertions: Recognizes this as email sequence work
Does not use Suede Social content patterns to write an email sequence

evals.prompt: I want to turn our new pricing guide into a LinkedIn carousel. It has 9 negotiation tactics for SaaS buyers. Help me structure the slides.
evals.expected_output: Should load references/carousel-frameworks.md and pick a framework before writing slides. A list of nine named tactics can map to Hack List or Value-Stack, but the choice must be justified. It should produce a slide-by-slide structure with an exact-count cover, one named tactic per slide, a synthesis, and one CTA. It should verify current LinkedIn document-post requirements before specifying upload behavior. Any promised count must be delivered and every claim must be sourced. It should define success from the campaign objective using the current metrics available, such as completion, saves, qualified replies, profile visits, or follows, rather than declaring one metric universally superior.
assertions: Loads or applies the carousel-frameworks reference
Selects an appropriate framework (Hack List or Value-Stack) with a stated reason before drafting slides
Slide 1 is written as a standalone scroll-stopper with the count or contrarian claim
One tactic/idea per slide, each named
Final slide has a synthesis and exactly one CTA
Applies LinkedIn document-post guidance (PDF, post text as its own hook)
Does not invent stats or pad the tactic count
